original_text:
If you haven't got real-time Data Engineering experience
Here's how you can make your own project for FREE !

Here’s a step-by-step guide to take you from raw data to a Power BI dashboard-all with FREE cloud tools. No more excuses. 

If you want to stand out, build and share real work.

Here’s how you do it 👇

1️⃣ Source Data (Python + Public Datasets)

Objective: Ingest real-world data into your pipeline.

- Use Python (`requests` or `pandas`) to fetch open datasets (CSV/JSON)
- Good sources: datahub.io, Google Dataset Search, Kaggle
- Save data locally or push to Azure Data Lake Gen2 / DBFS

(example)
python
import pandas as pd
url = "https://lnkd.in/gc7rWW-K"
df = pd.read_csv(url)
df.to_csv("global_temp.csv", index=False)

2️⃣ Transform in Databricks (PySpark)

Objective: Clean and process data at scale using Spark.

- Upload your CSV to Databricks (Community Edition is FREE)
- Open a notebook, clean and join data with PySpark
- Save as Delta table or write to external storage

(example)
python
df = spark.read.csv("/FileStore/global_temp.csv", header=True, inferSchema=True)
df_cleaned = df.filter("Mean > 0").withColumnRenamed("Mean", "MeanTemperature")
df_cleaned.write.format("delta").save("/mnt/processed/global_temp")


3️⃣ Load to Online Data Warehouse

Objective: Store clean data for analytics/reporting.

- Set up Azure SQL Database (free tier)
- Use Databricks JDBC or pyodbc to load clean data

(example)
python
df_cleaned.write \
.format("jdbc") \
.option("url", "jdbc:sqlserver://.database.windows.net:1433;database=") \
.option("dbtable", "dbo.GlobalTemperature") \
.option("user", "") \
.option("password", "") \
.mode("overwrite") \
.save()

4️⃣ Build Dashboards in Power BI

Objective: Visualize data and derive insights.

- Open Power BI Desktop
- Connect to Azure SQL
- Create line charts, KPIs, slicers
- Publish to Power BI Service (optional)


Project Structure:
- /data → raw datasets (CSV/JSON)
- /sql → transformation logic
- /notebooks → Databricks notebooks
- /tests → validation scripts
- README.md → overview + setup


Key Skills You Practice:
• Python scripting
• PySpark transformations
• Databricks workflows
• Azure SQL integration
• Power BI reporting
• Cloud-native workflow


You can use other tools like ADF for ingestion, key-vault for better security and airflow for scheduling your pipeline.


💡 Add this project to your portfolio or use it in interviews. All tools are free or have generous tiers. No paid subscriptions.


Need help setting this up or want feedback on your repo? 
Connect 1:1 here ➡️ https://lnkd.in/gH4DeYb4


♻️ Found this useful? Repost it to help others!
➕ Follow for more daily Data Engineering guides.

ai_analysis.summary: The post presents a portfolio-oriented project that moves public CSV or JSON data from Python ingestion through Databricks and PySpark transformation, Delta table or external-storage output, Azure SQL Database loading, and Power BI reporting. It also proposes a repository layout containing raw data, SQL logic, notebooks, validation scripts, and documentation. Python can save raw data locally or push it to Azure Data Lake Gen2 or DBFS, while the Azure SQL examples contain incomplete connection and credential values, so the snippets are illustrative rather than fully runnable as shown. Although the post frames the project as a way to gain real-time data engineering experience, it does not describe streaming or real-time processing.
topics: Optional ingestion, security, and scheduling tools
subtopics: Fetching public CSV and JSON datasets with requests or pandas
Saving raw data locally, in Azure Data Lake Gen2, or in DBFS
Cleaning and joining data with PySpark
Writing Delta tables or external storage
Loading data into Azure SQL with JDBC or pyodbc
Creating Power BI Desktop and Power BI Service reports
Organizing notebooks, SQL, tests, and raw data in a repository
Using ADF for ingestion, Key Vault for security, and Airflow for scheduling

interview_questions.question: Describe the end-to-end data flow proposed by the project.
interview_questions.answer:
Python ingests public CSV or JSON data into local storage, Azure Data Lake Gen2, or DBFS.
Databricks and PySpark clean and join the data before it is written as a Delta table or to external storage.
Azure SQL Database stores the clean data, and Power BI connects to it for reporting.

interview_questions.question: How would you use pandas to read a public CSV dataset and save a local copy?
interview_questions.answer:
The example uses pandas.read_csv with the dataset URL.
The DataFrame is written to global_temp.csv with to_csv and index=False.

interview_questions.question: How would you read, clean, and save a CSV as a Delta table with PySpark?
interview_questions.answer:
Spark reads /FileStore/global_temp.csv with a header and inferred schema.
The Mean column is filtered for positive values and renamed to MeanTemperature.
The cleaned DataFrame is written with format set to delta and a processed output path.

interview_questions.question: How can a cleaned Spark DataFrame be loaded into Azure SQL Database?
interview_questions.answer:
The JDBC writer specifies the SQL Server URL, database, destination table, username, and password.
The example uses overwrite mode for the destination table.
The post also identifies pyodbc and Key Vault as loading and security options without providing a complete implementation.

interview_questions.question: How would you turn the Azure SQL output into a Power BI report?
interview_questions.answer:
Power BI Desktop connects to the Azure SQL Database.
The report can include line charts, KPIs, and slicers.
Publishing the report to Power BI Service is optional.

interview_questions.question: What repository structure can be used to make this data engineering project portfolio-ready?
interview_questions.answer:
Raw datasets are kept in the data directory.
SQL logic and Databricks notebooks are stored separately.
The tests directory is reserved for validation scripts, and README.md documents the overview and setup.
